- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.77) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.27) or shows sharp drops, model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk aversion.
- After a price spike, model frequently overshoots in the next few days; apply a downward correction of 1–3% for the immediate follow-up period.
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome over 3–5 days, consider mean reversion bias — increase forecast slightly to align with recent upward momentum.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is volatile or mixed (alternating 0.53/0.27), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth out extremes and anchor to 14-day moving average of history.
- When sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from 0.80 to 0.00), model often fails to adjust quickly; delay forecast correction until sentiment stabilizes or next 3–5 days.
